idiom_name: one driver plus an algebra (one combine per case; foldLeft/foldRight/of the base functor)
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: fix the case set of the shape (empty/cons, leaf/node, each AST constructor), write the algebra as a total function from one layer of cases to the carrier, and let a single driver replace each layer with the algebra's result. Two choices must be made explicit rather than inherited from a spelling: direction and strictness (a right fold with a non-strict combine short-circuits and consumes as little as it must; a left fold accumulates strictly and needs an identity), and the identity element for the empty case. For a user-defined recursive type the driver is the catamorphism over the base functor: cata(algebra) recurses into the recursive positions and applies the algebra on the way back, which is the same driver for every consumer of that type. Choose a hand-written loop only when the platform's fold is missing, when the combine needs an escape hatch the fold does not offer, or when the abstraction's cost is measurably too high.
code_sketch:
# list form
fold_left(init, op, xs)  = ((init op x1) op x2) ...        # strict, needs identity
fold_right(op, init, xs) = x1 op (x2 op (... init))       # lazy combine may stop early
fold_map(f, xs)          = fold_left(mempty, mappend, map(f, xs))   # monoid form

# structural form (catamorphism over a base functor)
cata(algebra, layer):
    match layer:
        Empty      -> algebra.empty
        Leaf x     -> algebra.leaf(x)
        Node l, r  -> algebra.node(cata(algebra, l), cata(algebra, r))
pitfalls: Choosing a left fold, a right fold or a parallel reduce for a non-associative combine: the three disagree and the vocabulary usually hides which direction was chosen.
A wrong identity (0 for a minimum, an empty string for a join that needs a separator) corrupts exactly the empty case, which tests over non-empty data never exercise.
A non-total algebra with a catch-all branch: adding a case is then absorbed by the default instead of reported, and the fold silently produces the wrong carrier.

A lazy right fold with a strict combine: the non-strictness of foldr means it builds a chain of suspended calls that overflow the stack on long structures; use a strict left fold or a trampolined right fold.
Testing only non-empty structures: the identity element is only exercised on the empty case, so tests that use only non-empty inputs never catch a wrong identity.

Folding a streaming or infinite structure with a strict fold: the fold attempts full traversal instead of the short-circuit the right-fold with non-strict combine would provide; choose foldMap or a dedicated find/any primitive.

Confusing fold with a visitor: a fold sees only the children's folded results, never the original children or the layer's position in the tree; use a paramorphism or zygomorphism when that context is needed.

Wrong move: reducing into a persistent map with foldl and Map.insert (or foldMap with HashMap's monoid union) -> each step copies or unions the whole carrier and the fold degrades to quadratic time -> instead build with fromList, a mutable insert loop, or a chunked/balanced union, and measure the fold on the real collection size.

Wrong move: reducing with a lazy foldl in a lazy language -> the accumulator is never forced, a chain of thunks proportional to the input builds up and the fold fails with a space leak or stack overflow on large data -> instead use the strict foldl' (or an explicit strict accumulator), which is why the standard libraries ship both.

Wrong move: spelling every accumulation as a reduce/fold, including plain map/filter cases and search-with-early-exit -> the lambda hides the intent, implies an order-sensitivity that is not needed and cannot stop, so readers audit a loop where a named operation states the answer -> instead use map, filter, any/find or a loop, and reserve the fold for genuine monoidal accumulation.
